subject: Laos
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Mekong. The page gives two lengths: the infobox says 4,350 km and the lead says an estimated 4,909 km; the episode uses only the lead's figure and names it as an estimate. The river is drawn from the pinned Natural Earth rivers layer, not by hand. The upper Mekong lies in China (where it is officially called the Lancang) and the frames avoid Tibet and disputed areas: China is neither filled nor outlined, and is named only in narration and a caption. Cities used as markers (Vientiane, Phnom Penh, Can Tho) and the Tonlé Sap lake come from the map data.

claims.text: From its headwaters on the Tibetan Plateau the Mekong runs through Southwest China (where it is officially called the Lancang River), Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and southern Vietnam: six countries.
The Mekong is the world's twelfth-longest river and the third-longest in Asia, with an estimated length of 4,909 km.
In the upper Mekong basin, a stretch of some 2,200 km, the river drops 4,500 m before it enters the lower basin at the Golden Triangle.
The Mekong defines the Laos–Thailand border for some 850 km as it flows first east, passing Vientiane, then turns south.
At Phnom Penh the river is joined by the Tonlé Sap river and lake system; when the Mekong floods, the flow reverses, with the floodwaters flowing up the Tonlé Sap.
South of Phnom Penh the Bassac River branches off the Mekong, the beginning of the Mekong Delta; the rivers enter Vietnam shortly after and the Mekong is called the Tiền River there.
The construction of hydroelectric dams along the Mekong in the 2000s through the 2020s has caused serious problems for the river's ecosystem, including the exacerbation of drought.
